appraisal_events.evidence: « vous pourriez passer vos journées avec Elstir qui est un homme de génie »; « Mme de Cambremer trouvait avec raison que le charme spirituel d'Elstir était plus grand »
appraisal_events.explanation: Mme de Cambremer praises Elstir as a man of genius with superior spiritual charm; the narrator explicitly endorses this judgment as correct ('avec raison'), locally elevating Elstir even as he explains why love makes such objective comparisons irrelevant to his feelings.

status_effects.explanation: Elstir is affirmed, without irony, as a genius of superior intelligence and spiritual charm, a judgment the narrator endorses as correct.

ambiguities: Brichot and Mme Verdurin are mentioned only as figures whose ordinary social continuity (Brichot still dining, Mme Verdurin still receiving for years to come) underscores the injustice of Albertine's early death; this is used for reflection on mortality rather than to evaluate or reposition Brichot or Mme Verdurin themselves, so they were not scored.
The narrator's anger at receiving Mme Verdurin's invitation ('je jetai avec colère') reflects the pain of the reminder, not a judgment of Mme Verdurin, so no event was recorded for her.
The passage is sustained retrospective interior mourning without a staged social scene, so le narrateur was not scored as an in-scene participant despite being the emotional center of the passage.
